results.summary_before: This design is a 4-bit synchronous counter with a fully decoded hex output for a 7-segment display. It uses 29 2-input NAND gates for decoding, based on a minimized design from Kim Oyhus. The counter has an active-high enable and asynchronous reset, and counts on the positive clock edge. It requires no external hardware beyond the standard demo board.

results.summary_before: The design is a 16-microphone delay-and-sum beamformer that processes PDM inputs and outputs beamformed audio via I2S. It expects a 3.072 MHz bit clock and 48 kHz LR clock, and can use up to 16 digital microphones. Documentation is minimal placeholder text, so the internal beamforming details and test procedure are not described. The project is notable for targeting a high microphone count in a small digital design.

The documentation is minimal and emphasizes the destructive risk if misused.

results.summary_before: This is an 8-bit direct digital synthesizer (DDS) that generates a digitized sine wave with user-defined frequency. The frequency is set by an 8-bit phase increment loaded via input pins, and the output is an 8-bit amplitude sample updated every clock cycle. An external R-2R ladder DAC is required to convert the digital output to an analog sine wave. The design is based on standard DDS principles and can produce frequencies up to about 33 MHz at a 66 MHz clock.

results.summary_before: This analog project implements a voltage reference that compensates for temperature and supply voltage variations. It is designed by the LPCAS lab at IIT Gandhinagar. Testing requires precise temperature control using a TEC module and measurement of output voltages with high-impedance probes. Silicon test reports indicate partial success: one reference produced expected voltage but startup was sometimes strange, while the second reference appeared stuck at a low voltage.

results.summary_before: Spacewar is a scaled-down version of the classic Spacewar game written in Verilog, targeting VGA video output and audio. It reads a SNES-style gamepad over a clocked serial interface and also provides a PWM audio output and XY scope outputs. The pinout matches the Tiny VGA, TT Audio and Gamepad PMOD conventions, so external VGA, audio, SNES controller and scope hardware are required. The documentation is thin: testing is listed as 'Cocotb coming soon' and no silicon results are reported.
